problem: Zero-shot object navigation agents pretrained on ImageNav (e.g. ZSON) can solve the pretext task from layout/view matching alone, so they neglect semantics (semantic neglect). This limits object navigation and especially instance-level navigation with detailed descriptions.
motivation: Real-life applications need navigation to a specific object instance, not any object of a category. Pilot studies show a layout-only agent (Sobel edges, trainable ResNet-50) matches semantic agents on ImageNav, so the pretext task does not force semantic learning. The text-goal vs image-goal granularity gap at inference further hurts.
key_idea: Improve semantic perception of an ImageNav-pretrained agent via a semantic perception module on CLIP features, entropy-selected goal views with relaxed pitch/yaw reward, and retrieval-based expansion of text goals with image embeddings at inference.
insight: ImageNav success does not imply semantic understanding, so architecture and training must explicitly prioritize semantics. Ablation (Table 3): the perspective reward relaxation hurts the vanilla ZSON agent (12.7 to 10.8 SR) but helps greatly once the SPM agent is used (ImageNav-goal SR 16.5 to 22.0; ObjectNav SR 35.0 to 42.4), so the components are complementary. SEI matters: replacing image goals directly with text embeddings gives 6.6 SR versus 16.5 with retrieval expansion.
method: Semantic-Prioritized agent: a frozen CLIP encoder on the observation gives semantic observation z_S, alongside a learnable ResNet-50 (OVRL-initialized) observation embedding z_O and a frozen CLIP goal embedding z_G

Semantic Perception Module (SPM): an MLP bottleneck taking z_G and z_S and outputting a low-dimensional semantic perception embedding z_SP (C2 < 2*C1), fed with z_O and the previous action to a recurrent PPO actor-critic policy

Entropy-minimized Goal View Selection: render goal views at multiple yaw/pitch angles, and select those minimizing CLIP zero-shot class-probability entropy over 6 object categories (10 lowest-entropy candidates, 4 sampled per episode), which removes wall/room ambiguous goals

Perspective Reward Relaxation: pitch-varied goal views plus a modified reward that only requires the yaw angle (Y-axis quaternion component) to match, ignoring pitch, and does not demand exact view matching

Semantic Expansion Inference (SEI): build a support set of about 0.1M dissimilar goal-image CLIP embeddings (cosine threshold 0.8, no category labels); at test time the text embedding retrieves a softmax-similarity-weighted sum of these image embeddings as the goal
ZSIN benchmark: HM3D text-goal instance navigation, built from the IIN dataset with CogVLM-generated intrinsic and extrinsic attribute descriptions (1,000 episodes, 795 instances, 36 scenes)

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 (learnable, OVRL-init) + frozen CLIP encoders + MLP SPM + recurrent policy, trained with PPO
setting.training_data: ZSON's 7.2M HM3D ImageNav episodes (no object annotations); goal views selected by CLIP entropy; support set of about 0.1M image embeddings from goal images
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MOVE_FORWARD, TURN_LEFT, TURN_RIGHT, STOP, LOOK_UP, LOOK_DOWN

numbers.extra: Habitat 2022 challenge dataset, 2000 episodes, 6 categories; average of three seeds; no mapping/LLM

results: PSL reaches 42.4 SR / 19.2 SPL on zero-shot HM3D ObjectNav, above ZSON (25.5) and ESC (39.2, LLM+mapping). On text-goal instance navigation it gets 16.5 SR versus ZSON 10.6, and on image-goal instance navigation 23.0 SR versus ZSON 14.6 and FGPrompt 9.9, close to supervised OVRL-V2 in SPL (11.4 vs 11.8).
limitations: Absolute instance navigation success remains low (16.5% SR text-goal)
The text-goal instance benchmark uses descriptions auto-generated by CogVLM, which may be noisy
Entropy-based view selection relies on only 6 object categories, and the paper does not test on real robots
